newsitem.title: UK: IRA forces abandon mine in Catholic Belfast area.
newsitem.headline: IRA forces abandon mine in Catholic Belfast area.

text.p: Outlawed IRA guerrillas said on Saturday they had abandoned a defused landmine in a Catholic area of west Belfast in what was their first operation since Labour's landslide British election win on May 1.
A telephone caller using an Irish Republican Army identity codeword told Downtown radio station that their fighters had dumped the device "because of civilian activity in the area."

The telephone caller did not specify the target. The IRA has frequently placed landmines in nationalist Catholic areas aimed at passing British security force patrols in the predominantly Protestant province.

U.S. President Bill Clinton on Thursday urged the IRA to lay down its arms and said it had to compromise in order to join multi-party peace talks aimed at ending three decades of bloody conflict over the future of the pro-British province.
Shortly after winning power new Prime Minister Tony Blair allowed the resumption of talks between government officials and the IRA's Sinn Fein political wing.
But Blair made clear the talks could only take place if the IRA refrained from using violence. Two rounds of talks have been held in the past ten days and another is due soon.

The caller said the IRA's "engineers" had made the bomb safe before abandoning it in a white van in the Poleglass area of west Belfast. Police said that they were aware of the phone call but gave no further details.
The last recorded IRA action in the province was a sniper attrack which seriously wounded a policewoman in Londonderry city on April 10.
The IRA, which disrupted the run-up to the election, is fighting to end British rule in the province.
